dedupe_keys.name: aquacrop fao crop water productivity model

description: AquaCrop is FAO's crop growth model for the yield response of herbaceous crops to water, built by the Land, Soil and Water Division to address food security and to assess how environment and management affect production. It is designed for situations where water limits yield and deliberately uses few explicit parameters and mostly intuitive inputs that users can derive with simple calculations. From daily climate, crop, soil and management data it simulates the soil water balance, crop development and yield under rainfed, supplemental, deficit and full irrigation, which makes it a standard tool for estimating irrigation water requirements and evaluating irrigation strategies. FAO distributes version 7.3 free of charge as a Windows program with a graphical interface and database, as stand-alone programs for Windows, Linux and Mac that run predefined project text files for batch and parallel runs, and as Python source code; release notes and publications are on the same page. It is site-independent and applied worldwide at field scale. The licence is not stated on the page. Caveats: it models herbaceous crops at field scale, not canals or irrigation networks, and its outputs depend on local calibration of crop and soil parameters. Simulation uses: irrigation demand for water-allocation and capacity planning, drought and climate adaptation studies, and optimisation of irrigation schedules. It is often combined with the Global Map of Irrigation Areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas) and with FAO CROPWAT, a separate irrigation-planning program.
